title: Dual-rate per-direction token pricing + streaming minima experiment (hosted API)
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Current hosted API pricing uses a single combined per-token rate (input+output bundled) plus a streaming path that has per-minute billing and an implied minimum for small streams. Enterprise customers and sales-negotiated contracts often request clarity on directional costs and predictable minimums.

Hypothesis: Introducing a per-direction (input token vs output token) rate with an explicit streaming minimum (time-based and token-based) will (1) improve margin transparency for high-output workloads, (2) reduce bill shock for low-latency streaming customers by making minimums explicit, and (3) provide better levers for sales to structure enterprise contracts. We expect high-output, generation-heavy clients to prefer lower output-token rates and high-input workloads (classification/embedding prep) to benefit from lower input-token rates.

Goal: Run an A/B/C experiment across new signups and a small slice of existing customers to evaluate conversion, revenue per MAU, average invoice variance, and churn for the hosted API over a 4-week experiment window.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implemented pricing variants in billing simulator and billing pipeline with clear logging per-direction. 2) Data collection of per-customer token direction breakdowns enabled. 3) Experiment runs for minimum 4 weeks with >=100 active customers in each cohort or 95% power to detect 8% change in revenue/MAU. 4) No >5% increase in support incidents attributable to confusing invoices. 5) Post-experiment recommendation (roll forward / iterate / cancel) documented and approved by PM + Finance + Sales leadership.
experiment_design:
Variants:
- Control (V0): existing combined per-token rate (baseline).
- Variant A (V1): Separate input token rate = $0.0008/token, output token rate = $0.0020/token; streaming charged per-second with a $0.10 per-minute minimum.
- Variant B (V2): Lower output token rate $0.0016/token with a per-stream fixed minimum of 50 tokens or $0.05, whichever is higher.
- Variant C (V3): Per-direction rates with tiered discounts above monthly thresholds (e.g., >50M output tokens -> 10% discount) and streaming billed as per-second with explicit 30-second free warmup for interactive sessions.

Cohorts:
- New signups only (50%) + small percent of production customers (25%) segmented by monthly token usage: Low (<100k), Medium (100k-5M), High (>5M).

Duration: 28 days active collection + 7 days for billing reconciliation.

Edge handling: Enterprise contracts on negotiation or reserved capacity will be opt-out by default; Sales can opt-in customers via the sales portal. Any customer with a pending security questionnaire referencing billing must be excluded until Legal confirms answer templates.
metrics_tracking:
Primary metrics:
- Revenue per active customer (rev/MAU) by cohort and variant.
- Average invoice variance (month-over-month) and frequency of unexpected spikes.
- Conversion rate for free-to-paid signups.
- Churn / retention at 30 days.

Secondary metrics:
- Support ticket volume and NPS signal for billing clarity.
- Unit economics: gross margin per 1M tokens served (directional).

Measurement plan: Use billing-analytics dashboard (billing-2025.02) with a daily export to the pricing experiment spreadsheet. Statistical significance target: 95% with minimum detectable effect of 8% on rev/MAU.
